newsitem.title: USA: FUND VIEW - Montgomery Intl Growth looks to Europe.
newsitem.headline: FUND VIEW - Montgomery Intl Growth looks to Europe.

text.p: John Boich, portfolio manager of the Montgomery International Growth Fund, is bullish on profit prospects for companies in continental Europe.
According to data that Boich has collected, earnings forecasts are especially robust for France, with average growth expected at 17.6 percent, and for Italy, at 17.25 percent.
The two countries are among the top weighted in the fund's portfolio, with France at 10.98 percent, the second biggest regional holding, and Italy at 6.29 percent, fourth biggest.
In searching for stocks, Boich looks closely at macreconomic conditions in regions around the world, then looks at companies that could benefit, with a view at sector strength.
"We still see declining interest rates," he said, referring to continental Europe. "There's lower capacity utilization; they're a trough economy," which should help propel earnings growth.
The fund focuses on mid-cap stocks, with market capitalization stretching from about $500 million up to about $6 billion.

Currently Europe represents about 70 percent of the portfolio, up from 60 percent a year ago. Japan remains the top regional holding at 14.74 percent, but that's down from about 20 percent a year ago.
Boich said technology is a favorite industry sector, with earnings expected to grow nearly 20 percent next year on average.
"Outside the United States, there are signs that the audience for personal computers will be exploding," Boich said. "PC penetration in continental Europe and Japan is much lower than in the U.S."

One favorite within the sector is cellular telephone manufacturers, including Finland's Nokia Ab Oy, one of the fund's top holdings, and Sweden's LM Ericsson AB. He sees much larger worldwide market penetrations ahead.
Other top industry holdings include retail trade at 11 percent, and pharmacy/drugs at 8.91 percent.
The portfolio of the $20 million fund has about 60 stocks, with most comprising about two percent of the fund, and about seven percent in cash, up from two to three percent in cash.
The top five holdings include: Danzas Holding, Dixons Group Plc, Gucci Group NV, Sandoz AG, and Nokia.
According to Lipper Analytical Services, the fund returned 15.03 percent year to date, versus 8.01 percent for the average international fund.
For the second half of 1995, it returned 11.42 percent versus 6.84 percent for the average fund. The fund began in June 1995.
